sections.h2: Salt Lake City east and west
sections.html:
As Utah's capital and the county seat, Salt Lake City anchors the valley. Its 110.8 square miles fill the valley's northeast corner, bounded by the Wasatch Range on one side, the Oquirrh Mountains on the other and the Great Salt Lake off to the northwest. The Jordan River crosses the city, average elevation is 4,327 feet, and the 2020 census found 199,723 residents.

Neighborhoods on the east side, such as the Avenues, 9th and 9th, Yalecrest, Federal Heights and Sugar House, lean more affluent. Poplar Grove, Rose Park and Glendale on the west side lean more working-class and diverse. Yalecrest and Rose Park are different worlds, so think about which side yours is on before settling on a price.

Brigham Young led Latter-day Saint pioneers here in 1847. The place was incorporated in 1851, platted in 1857 and named Great Salt Lake City until 1868, when Great was dropped. Rail arrived in 1870, and statehood in 1896 made it the capital.

Many Victorian-era homes stand in the Avenues, a historic district. Older houses cost more to maintain, and an owner facing a long repair list may find a cash sale simpler.

sections.h2: The Wasatch Fault and your house
sections.html:
Along the mountain front, the Wasatch Fault has a Salt Lake City segment beneath the city, which last broke roughly 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years are put at 57 percent, and the ground could shift by as much as 20 feet at the surface. Buildings across the valley took damage when a magnitude 5.7 quake struck near Magna on March 18, 2020.

  • At least 42 percent of Wasatch Front buildings are at risk of moderate to severe damage in a strong quake.
  • Liquefaction is a risk where buildings sit on soft lake sediments.
  • Gas, electric and water lines are expected to be damaged after a large quake.

Quake risk is no barrier to selling. When a house shows damage from the 2020 quake or from settling, selling as-is is often easier than repairing first.

sections.h2: Winters and what they do to a roof
sections.html:
The seasons swing hard, from cold winters to hot summers. At the airport, precipitation averages about 15.5 inches and snowfall roughly 52 inches, with about 127 days at or below freezing. Mean daily highs are 38.6 degrees in January and 94.0 degrees in July.

The freeze count is what matters for a house. Roofs, gutters, sprinkler lines and exposed pipes endure repeated freezing and thawing, which makes buyers wary of deferred roof or plumbing work.

Each residential rental in the city needs its own current business license. Single and double family homes and similar rentals fall under the Landlord/Tenant Initiative, known as the Good Landlord Program. Joining can cut per-unit fees by up to 95 percent. The ordinance began on September 1, 2011.

Heirs of a former rental and owners weary of managing a duplex run into this. Tenants can stay through a cash purchase, and it is fine to ask us how that touches the lease and your license.

Nightly rentals need a city business license and are limited to approved zoning districts. One person may hold just one short-term rental license in the city.

  • A license covers one property and one dwelling unit.
  • The minimum stay is two consecutive nights.
  • A unit may be rented for no more than 200 nights per calendar year.
  • In a building with more than 11 units, up to 10 percent may be covered.
  • Condominium units need an HOA authorization letter.

MU2, MU3, D1 and GMU are among the approved districts. Look up your address's zoning before promising a buyer short-term rental income, and call Business Licensing at (801) 535-7980 for fees and dates.

City homes are billed by the county. Value is fixed on January 1, and an owner-occupied primary residence is exempt from 45 percent of the value of its buildings and up to one acre of land.

Tax sales usually happen on the fourth Thursday of May.
File form BE01 with evidence of what the house is worth. A late appeal can be taken up to March 31 of the following year, though only for narrow reasons, so file on time.

Back taxes will not stop a sale. Delinquent taxes are certified each March 15 and head toward the May tax sale, so waiting only makes the situation harder. The title company pulls the balance with penalties and pays it out of your proceeds at closing. For a payoff figure ahead of time, ask the county Treasurer.

The standard Utah purchase contract has sellers disclose known problems, typically on a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form. Your title or escrow company can say which forms fit your sale. Topics include roof leaks, flooding and drainage, mold, structural or soil problems, permits and HOA details.

Even heirs who never lived there should report what they know, and a Utah real estate attorney can answer doubts. Property records sit with the county Recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, which keeps hours Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Listing, selling yourself or selling for cash
sections.html:
Owners here usually compare three paths: an agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. Condition, timing and tenants decide which fits.

Listing works best for a well-kept house in a strong location when you can wait out showings. Cash fits deferred repairs, rentals with tenants, probate property or a firm closing date. Ask for an offer, set it against your likely net from a listing, and decline if it falls short. You owe nothing.

  1. Describe the house, its condition and any tenants.
  2. We review the details and make an offer.
  3. Accept, and a title company runs the closing and records the deed with the county.

Before the first call, collect the deed, the latest tax notice, any lease and your rental or short-term rental license if you have one. Missing items can usually be handled through the title company.

faqs.q: What county is Salt Lake City in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The city is also the county seat, so the county Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder serve its homeowners.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake City property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, with a penalty of the greater of 2.5 percent or $10, reduced to the greater of 1 percent or $10 if paid by January 31.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: September 15, or 45 days from the notice date if that is later. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization from August 1 and need a BE01 form with evidence of value.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my Salt Lake City house?
faqs.a: Yes. Every residential rental property needs a valid business license for each location. The Good Landlord Program can cut per-unit fees by up to 95 percent.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Salt Lake City?
faqs.a: Only in approved zoning districts and with a city business license. Stays must be at least two nights, and each unit is capped at 200 rental nights a year.
